mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of FEDFUNDS-tightening episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply-chain shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which historically precedes wage inflation and central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of overheating episodes, or the effect disappears during a geopolitical shock.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of at least 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a tech-driven market rally.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which historically has been associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 65% of dual-trigger episodes, or the effect reverses during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase of at least 2% in both HOUST (new single-family houses sold) and RSAFS (retail sales) month-over-month signals a broad-based acceleration in consumer spending, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise ≥2% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of dual-trigger episodes, or the effect is absent during a rate hike cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS (nonfarm payrolls) above the prior 12-month average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market strength, which supports corporate margin expansion and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.5% in INDPRO for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing rebound, which improves earnings visibility and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises ≥0.5% MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a global supply shock.
